label: Jennifer Hart Weed, Religious Language §2a: Ayer 1946: the notion of a person whose essential…
locator: §2a, "But the notion of a person whose essential attributes are non-empirical is not an intelligible notion at all."
interpretation: Ayer, LTL 2nd ed., ch. VI, p. 144, quoted verbatim by the IEP entry: the theological consequence of the criterion. Attribution reading on a secondary witness.
attribution: The passage states in a verbatim quotation of Ayer 1946, p. 144, that the notion of a person with non-empirical essential attributes is not intelligible and that a word used to name such a person symbolizes nothing unless its sentences express empirically verifiable propositions, which is the premise.
